answer: For every seal taken the hunter cuts a notch in the tally stick, and the stick is split between hunter and village elder so neither can cheat the count. A ivory notch carved in an afternoon fails the stick: at the pulse of the cut the wood must show a season of weather, and a fresh notch shines pale against the old ones. Forging the tally means hunting for two winters, faking 140 notches and paying 9,300, and the terrace half held by the elder is matched at every division of the catch, so a seal that was never taken earns no share.
